pages.text: Multiplying by `w` turns and stretches. Here the arrow 1, 1 long at 0°, turns through 40° and grows 3 times as long, which makes `w = 3∠40°`.

pages.why: Multiplying by `2∠50°` turns `4∠25°` through 50° and stretches it 2 times. Its arc is 25° with 50° laid on the end, `25° + 50° = 75°`, and its length is `4 × 2 = 8`. So the answer is `8∠75°`.

pages.name: 10 ÷ (3 + j4)
pages.task: Work out `10 ÷ (3 + j4)` in polar form. `3 + j4` is `5∠53.13°`.
pages.why: `10` is `10∠0°`, and `3 + j4` is `5∠53.13°`. Divide the lengths, `10 ÷ 5 = 2`, and take the angles away, `0° − 53.13° = −53.13°`. So the answer is `2∠−53.13°`. Its parts are `2 cos(−53.13°) = 1.2` across and `2 sin(−53.13°) = −1.6` up, so it is `1.2 − j1.6`, as the conjugate lesson found.

pages.name: j2 × j2
pages.why: Multiply the lengths, `2 × 2 = 4`, and add the angles, `90° + 90° = 180°`. `4∠180°` points straight left, so it is `−4`. By parts, `j2 × j2 = j × j × 4 = −4`, the same.
